office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, covering school funding, the tax structure, housing rules, behavioral-health funding, transportation projects, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Appointed Democratic incumbent Zach Hall faces Republican Michelle Bennett, Mercer Island's police chief, after a close primary (44.5% to 43.0% in the King County count). The seat is on the ballot as both a short term and a full two-year term.

candidates.summary: Appointed in June 2025 and seeking election in his own right; Vice Chair of the House Environment & Energy Committee and a former Issaquah City Councilmember.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million [S4]
Frames public safety around first responders, gun-violence prevention, and behavioral-health interventions [S2]
Commits to cutting greenhouse gas emissions and moving away from fossil fuels faster [S2]

taxes.basis: Recorded yea on House final passage of the 2026 tax on income over $1 million; no further public statement on revenue found.

spending.basis: Calls for more school funding, protecting essential services, and investment in infrastructure, childcare and healthcare access.

housing.basis: Housing platform centers on supply and reforms that make it easier to finance and build homes faster; no tenant-protection or social-housing position stated.

safety.basis: Describes safety as first-responder support, gun-violence prevention, and behavioral-health and substance-use interventions that meet people where they are.

climate.basis: Commits to reducing emissions and transitioning away from fossil fuels faster; endorsed by WA Conservation Action and Sierra Club.

experience.basis: Appointed incumbent with one legislative session plus six years on a city council; a short record rather than long tenure.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and the WA State Stonewall Democrats; no direct statement found.

candidates.summary: Mercer Island police chief and former chief in Maple Valley and Sammamish, running for office for the first time on tax restraint and public safety.
highlights: Says Olympia passed "the largest tax increase in state history" and that police lack clear tools [S1]
Says state housing and zoning mandates do not work for every community [S2]
Endorsed by the King County Republican Party [S8]

taxes.basis: Opposes an income tax, criticizes recent tax increases in her pamphlet, and cites the new income tax as a reason for running.

spending.basis: Pledges to ensure state spending delivers measurable results, an accountability frame.

safety.basis: Police-chief candidate who says police lack tools to protect victims and wants drugs made illegal again, paired with pretrial diversion.

experience.basis: First run for office, though she brings a long law-enforcement executive career rather than a legislative record.

local-control.basis: Said Olympia dictating a city's housing zoning or affordable housing 'simply doesn't work for every community.'
